entries.title: Augmented reality: on the cusp of reality
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that over a billion smartphone users will create augmented reality (AR) content at least once in 2018, with three hundred million being monthly creators and tens of millions making and sharing content weekly.
entries.metric: smartphone users creating AR content at least once
entries.subject: Augmented reality

entries.title: The future of the smartphone: the era of invisible innovation
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that by the end of 2023, penetration of smartphones among adults in developed countries will surpass 90 percent, a five-percentage-point increase over 2018.
entries.subject: Smartphone penetration

entries.title: Smartphones are useful, but they can be distracting
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that 45 percent of global adult smartphone users in 2018 will worry they are using their phones too much for certain activities, and 45 percent of all adult smartphone users will try to limit their phone usage
entries.metric: adult smartphone users worried about overuse
entries.subject: Smartphone overuse

entries.title: Hitting the accelerator: the next generation of machine-learning chips
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that by the end of 2018, over 25 percent of all chips used to accelerate machine learning in the data center will be FPGAs (field programmable gate arrays) and ASICs (application-specific integrated circuits).
entries.metric: FPGA and ASIC share of data-center ML accelerator chips
entries.subject: Machine learning chips

entries.title: Machine learning: things are getting intense
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that in 2018, large and medium-sized enterprises will intensify their use of machine learning. The number of implementations and pilot projects using the technology will double compared with 2017, and they will have doubled again by 2020.
entries.metric: enterprise ML implementations and pilots vs 2017
entries.subject: Enterprise machine learning

entries.title: Live thrives in an online world
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that live broadcast and events will generate $545 billion in direct revenue in 2018, a one percent increase over the previous year.
entries.metric: direct revenue from live broadcast and events
entries.subject: Live events and broadcast

entries.title: Digital media: the subscription prescription
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that by the end of 2018, 50 percent of adults in developed countries will have at least two online-only media subscriptions, and by the end of 2020, that average will have doubled to four.
entries.metric: developed-country adults with 2+ online-only media subscriptions
entries.subject: Digital media subscriptions

entries.title: Is there an #adlergic epidemic? Ad blocking across media
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that 10 percent of North Americans over age 18 will be engaged in four or more multiple, simultaneous advertisement-blocking behaviors in 2018
entries.metric: North American adults with 4+ ad-blocking behaviors
entries.subject: Ad blocking

entries.title: The kids are alright: no tipping point in TV viewing trends for 18-24 year olds
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that traditional TV viewing ... among 18-24 year olds will decline by 5 to 15 percent per year in the US, Canada and the UK in both 2018 and 2019.
entries.metric: annual decline in traditional TV viewing, 18-24 year olds
entries.subject: Youth TV viewing

entries.title: Mobile-only: wireless home internet is bigger than you think
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that 20 percent of North Americans with internet access will get all of their home data access via cellular mobile networks (mobile-only) in 2018.
entries.metric: North Americans with mobile-only home internet
entries.subject: Mobile-only home internet

entries.title: Fasten your seatbelts: in-flight connectivity takes off
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that in 2018, one billion passenger journeys on planes (about a quarter of the total) will be on aircraft equipped with in-flight connectivity (IFC).
entries.subject: In-flight connectivity

notes: 17th edition by count from 2002. Published December 2017 (release date of the 2018 edition moved into the previous December; exact day not confirmed). Rank is the order in the report.
